note.explanation: Hazard signs tell people about dangers or safety rules in a particular area or on a chemical bottle. They help people notice the hazard and take the right precautions.
examples: A flame with “Highly flammable” warns that the material can catch fire easily.
A corrosive symbol warns that contact with the material can destroy living tissue.
note.checkAnswer: The sign warns that the material may cause suffocation or asphyxiation.
note.simple: A hazard sign is a warning picture or message. It tells you what danger to look out for and how to behave safely.
note.checkQuestion: What danger does a sign marked “Risk of asphyxiation” warn about?
note.title: Understanding Hazard Signs
steps: Look at the symbol and read the words on the sign.
Identify the danger or instruction it shows.
Take the required precaution and follow any safety instructions.
note.answer: Hazard signs warn people about dangers and indicate the precautions they must follow.

options: The material may catch fire easily
The material presents a radiation hazard
mcqs.stem: What does a flame sign labelled “Highly flammable” warn you about?
rationales: Correct: the flame sign and wording identify a fire hazard.
Incorrect: a corrosive sign warns about material that can damage living tissue.
Incorrect: a radiation symbol identifies a radiation hazard.
Incorrect: an asphyxiation warning identifies a suffocation hazard.

mcqs.stem: Which danger is identified by a sign that says “Risk of asphyxiation”?
rationales: Correct: asphyxiation means suffocation, often because of a lack of oxygen.
Incorrect: radiation has its own radiation hazard symbol.
Incorrect: corrosion is shown by the corrosive warning symbol.
Incorrect: an explosion symbol warns of an explosive hazard.

mcqs.stem: What hazard does the radiation symbol identify?
rationales: Correct: the symbol is used to warn of a radiation hazard.
Incorrect: a skull and crossbones identifies a toxic hazard in the figure.
Incorrect: a hot-surface symbol warns about heat.
Incorrect: a corrosive symbol warns of a corrosive material.

options: A place where hands must be sanitized
A place where lab coats must be worn
mcqs.stem: In the figure, what does the skull-and-crossbones sign marked “TOXIC HAZARD” indicate?
rationales: Correct: the sign is explicitly labelled “TOXIC HAZARD.”
Incorrect: a flame sign indicates a flammable hazard.
Incorrect: the hand-sanitizing symbol gives a hygiene instruction.
Incorrect: the lab-coat symbol gives a protective-clothing instruction.

options: Contact with the material can destroy living tissue
The material must be kept away from all light
The material is safe to touch
mcqs.stem: What danger does a corrosive warning sign indicate?
rationales: Correct: corrosive material can destroy living tissue on contact.
Incorrect: radiation is shown by the radiation hazard symbol.
Incorrect: this is not the meaning of the corrosive sign.
Incorrect: a corrosive warning means the material is hazardous, not safe to touch.

mcqs.stem: Which instruction is shown by the face-mask symbol in Fig. (13.1)?
rationales: Correct: the figure labels the symbol “Wear face mask.”
Incorrect: the hand-sanitizing symbol gives that instruction.
Incorrect: a crossed-out person marks restricted entry.
Incorrect: the hot-surface symbol warns about a hot surface.

written.text: A few decades ago, a tanker carrying poisonous chlorine gas leaked and the gas spread over a large area in Lahore. The accident killed a few persons as well as animals. Give some concrete proposals to avoid such an accident in future.
written.finalAnswer: Use clear toxic-gas warning signs on tankers and storage areas, inspect and maintain containers to prevent leaks, train staff in safe handling and emergency response, and alert nearby people promptly if a leak occurs.

modelAnswer: Display clear toxic-gas warning signs on tankers and storage areas.

If a leak occurs, promptly alert nearby people and move them away from the danger.

examTips: Short-answer questions may ask what a particular sign means or why signs are displayed; name the hazard and state the safety purpose.
A constructed response may ask you to identify radiation and asphyxiation signs. Name each sign and explain the danger it warns about.
For descriptive answers about signs, include both what the signs indicate and how they help people take precautions and avoid accidents.
When asked for examples of chemicals, give clear examples and do not confuse a hazard category, such as corrosive, with a particular chemical.
For full marks, connect each warning to its meaning: for example, corrosive means contact can destroy living tissue.

explain.title: Why hazard signs are needed
explain.body: “Proper warning signs ought to be posted on these areas to ensure that every person entering there must understand and act accordingly to maintain laboratory safety.” Signs make hazards visible to people who enter the laboratory.

explain.title: What signs tell you
explain.body: “These signs indicate that specific precautions must be observed according to the requirement of the sign posted there.” Read the words and identify the symbol so that you know which precaution is needed.

explain.title: Examples of warnings
explain.body: A flame sign warns of a flammable material, a skull and crossbones indicates a toxic hazard, a radiation symbol warns of radiation, and a corrosive symbol warns about corrosive material.

explain.title: Signs can give instructions too
explain.body: Some signs tell you what to do, such as wearing a lab coat or face mask, sanitizing hands, or allowing entry only to authorized personnel.

mistakes: Do not treat every hazard sign as if it means the same thing; identify the specific hazard or instruction.
Do not confuse toxic, corrosive, flammable and explosive hazards.
Do not only name a sign when asked why signs are posted; explain that they warn people and guide precautions.
Do not ignore instruction signs such as wearing protective clothing or restricting entry.
